summary: Reviewed the complete cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness against all eight Delta units and the relevant formal-model contracts. The seven authorized edits reconstruct the committed sources exactly (src/core/templates/workflows/explore.ts:32-35; src/core/templates/workflows/propose.ts:75,114), the frozen candidate prompts match the tracked generated surfaces, and the independently rerun 19 template/installation suites passed all 246 tests. The raw dialogues substantiate their reported bounded conversational outcomes, but required active investigation and consequential-feasibility handling lack behavior evidence. This is a verification failure, not an observed failure of the approved wording. HEAD remained unchanged and the project worktree remained clean.
findings: CRITICAL — Completeness/Correctness, G1 verification: active investigation of discoverable project facts is required by .xirang/changes/intent-solution-feasibility/tasks.md:3-5 and elements/explore-brainstorming.md:26, and implemented in src/core/templates/workflows/explore.ts:33. However, .xirang/changes/intent-solution-feasibility/evidence/dialogue-workflow.js:3-22 supplies the repository facts in user messages, and line 32 expressly prohibits every command except reading the frozen prompt. evidence/verification.md:42 confirms that actual project investigation was not exercised. The existing string checks in test/core/templates/explore-template.test.ts:16-29 do not establish investigation behavior. An Agent that always asks the user for readily available repository facts would still pass this experiment. Add bounded one-time behavior evidence with discoverable project facts and permitted read-only tools, retaining the actual calls and responses so the required investigation can be assessed; a new persistent test or a complete workflow replay is unnecessary.

CRITICAL — Completeness/Correctness, G2 verification: the changed feasibility policy requires delegation before confirming dependent design when consequential uncertainty remains, and disclosure of remaining uncertainty and its decision impact when execution is blocked or inconclusive (.xirang/changes/intent-solution-feasibility/elements/explore.md:25-29; src/core/templates/workflows/explore.ts:35). The sole experiment prohibits delegation (evidence/dialogue-workflow.js:32); its evidence scenario supplies a successful local result and a logical contradiction (lines 8-12), but no blocked or inconclusive execution result. evidence/verification.md:42 explicitly confirms that Experimenter delegation was not exercised. Inspection of every input in evidence/dialogues.json found no blocked/inconclusive execution case; the recorded result objects contain no tool/delegation trace. Also, git grep -n -E 'not every design needs|consequential feasibility|execution is blocked|results are inconclusive|Investigate facts available' HEAD -- test returned no matches. The evidence therefore cannot reject an Agent that never delegates unresolved feasibility questions or incorrectly treats a blocked experiment as resolved. Add a bounded one-time case permitting an observable Experimenter handoff and result consumption, including a blocked or inconclusive result; verify that dependent design is not prematurely confirmed and the remaining uncertainty and decision impact are explained. Existing sufficient-evidence dialogues already cover the no-new-experiment branch.
